domain_guidance.summary: Focuses on establishing clear, respectful dialogue with staff, patients, and interdisciplinary teams, fostering trust, and using effective listening and feedback techniques to improve collaboration and patient outcomes across clinical settings.

Encompasses understanding of health policy, regulatory standards, quality improvement, patient safety, and the broader organizational context that influences nursing practice and strategic decision‑making including reimbursement models, accreditation requirements, and emerging technology trends.

Addresses executive leadership functions such as vision setting, change management, ethical decision‑making, mentorship, and influencing organizational culture to achieve high‑quality patient care and staff engagement through strategic planning, resource allocation, and performance evaluation.

Covers financial management, budgeting, data analytics, operations oversight, and business acumen needed for nurse executives to align resources with organizational goals and sustain fiscal responsibility including contract negotiation, risk management, and strategic investment planning.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive early, bring two forms of ID, and have a printed copy of the exam confirmation. Use the provided calculator if allowed, manage time to answer all 175 questions, and review flagged items before submitting.

faq.answer_text: The NE-BC exam contains 175 multiple-choice questions. All items must be completed within the allotted 210-minute testing window. The linear format presents each question sequentially, so you cannot return to earlier items.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The exam uses a scaled scoring system from 200 to 500. A score of 350 is required to pass and earn the five-year NE-BC certification.
Test takers have 210 minutes to answer all 175 questions. The exam is administered in a single linear session, and the clock runs continuously from start to finish.
The non-member fee is $520. ANA members receive a reduced price of $395. Prices are listed on the ANCC certification page and must be paid before scheduling the exam.
faq.question_title: What is the cost for non-members?

editorial.overview: Administered by the American Nurses Credentialing Center, the Nurse Executive, Board Certified (NE-BC) credential validates senior nursing leaders’ expertise across four domains: Communication and Relationship Building, Knowledge of the Healthcare Environment, Leadership, and Business Skills. The linear, multiple-choice exam consists of 175 items completed in 210 minutes. A scaled score of 350 (out of 500) is required to earn the five-year certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the ANCC certification handbook and focus on each domain’s key concepts. Use practice questions to become comfortable with the linear, multiple-choice format. Allocate study time to cover communication strategies, regulatory environment, leadership models, and business finance. Join a study group or forum for peer discussion, and schedule a full-length mock exam to gauge pacing for the 210-minute window.
editorial.who_should_take: Current nurse executives, chief nursing officers, directors of nursing, and senior nurse managers who oversee clinical operations, strategic planning, and financial stewardship should pursue NE-BC to demonstrate executive competence within healthcare organizations.

exam_rules: Closed-book. No notes or reference materials permitted. On-screen calculator provided where applicable. 60-day waiting period required before retaking. MSN or APRN graduate degree required for advanced practice NP certifications.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Name must match ANCC registration exactly. RN license number required at check-in.

prerequisites.description: Current, active RN license in the US or its territories
2 years of experience in a nurse executive/administrator role at the nurse manager level or above
BSN or higher degree in nursing

renewal_options: Earn 75 CE credits (contact hours) every 5 years. CE credits must be relevant to the certification specialty. Submit renewal application via the ANCC certification portal. Maintain current, active RN license throughout certification period.

retake_policy.notes: Must wait 60 days before retaking. Full exam fee required for each retake attempt. Check ANCC website for current retake policies.

testing_centers.notes: Computer-based testing at Prometric test centers; online proctoring available for select exams
